title: Can the controller show each record was NOT accessed through the exposed key?
prepared_for: Piotr Reder — case 2 (synthetic): 'No entry is a claim, not a default'

propositions.section: 1 — What the submitted log records (record level)
propositions.statement: no read of orders record O-0417 attributed to key k_7f3a is recorded in the submitted access log during the exposure window
propositions.reason: the submitted log contains no read of O-0417 attributed to the key (documentary)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — documentary. The submitted orders log contains no read of O-0417 attributed to the exposed key. A fact about the LOG'S CONTENTS, read as submitted; it does NOT, on its own, establish real-world non-access — that is R-A-world, where the declared anchor and the undemonstrated capture bite.

propositions.section: 1 — What the submitted log records (record level)
propositions.statement: no read of invoices record I-0988 attributed to key k_7f3a is recorded in the submitted access log during the exposure window
propositions.reason: the submitted log contains no read of I-0988 attributed to the key (documentary)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — documentary. The submitted invoices log contains no entry reading I-0988 attributed to the key. A fact about the log's contents; the coverage gap that defeats the world-level claim (R-B-world) does not change what the log, as submitted, contains.

propositions.section: 1 — What the submitted log records (record level)
propositions.statement: no row-level read of customers record C-5521 attributed to key k_7f3a is recorded in the submitted access log during the exposure window
propositions.reason: no row-level read of C-5521 recorded — only a call-level query attributed to the key
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — documentary. The submitted customers log records only a CALL-level query (/v1/customers/search {postcode_prefix:'29'} at 01:40, no row ids) attributed to the key — no row-level read of C-5521. A fact about the log's contents; whether C-5521 was returned by that query is the world-level question (R-C-world).

propositions.section: 1 — What the submitted log records (record level)
propositions.statement: no read of addresses record A-7730 attributed to key k_7f3a is recorded in the submitted access log during the exposure window
propositions.reason: the submitted log contains no read of A-7730 attributed to the key (documentary)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — documentary. The submitted addresses log contains no read of A-7730 attributed to the key. A fact about the log's contents; that this log is unchained and db-admin-writable is what defeats the world-level claim (R-D-world), not the record-level reading.

propositions.section: 1 — What the submitted log records (record level)
propositions.statement: no read of invoices record I-3301 attributed to key k_7f3a is recorded in the submitted access log during the exposure window
propositions.reason: a read of I-3301 attributed to the key (declared) IS recorded at 03:05 — contradicts 'the log is silent'; record-level only
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED — bounded to the submitted record. The access log contains a read of I-3301 at 03:05 attributed to the key's prefix (a row-level entry on the hash-chained, anchored invoices log), so the claim that the log is silent on such a read is false. This is a claim about the RECORD, not the world. The attribution — that the read carries the api-key:k_7f3a prefix — is DECLARED, not independently verified, exactly as it is for R-A–R-D's ABSENCE of a read; the finding holds R-E's attribution to the same bar, not a lower one. What is contradicted is only that the log is silent; whether a real access occurred under that attribution is R-E-world.

propositions.section: 2 — What that does not establish about the world
propositions.statement: orders record O-0417 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the exposure window (real-world non-access, via the logged path, under the declared key scope)
propositions.reason: DECLARED, not supported — structure present, but anchor only simulated and capture not demonstrated (verified anchor + attribution are necessary, not sufficient)
propositions.basis: STRONGEST record, but DECLARED not supported. The logging STRUCTURE is present: logger-orders reported alive across the whole window, the orders log is hash-chained, contiguous and anchored with the config hash bound in, and there is no entry by the key (R-A-record). It stops short on two counts. (1) The anchor signatures and RFC-3161 tokens are simulated (a synthetic bundle), so the chain's trustworthiness currently rests on DECLARATION, not on an independently verifiable signature. (2) A continuous heartbeat shows the logger was UP, not that it CAPTURED every relevant access on this path (liveness is not capture). Independently verified anchor signatures, timestamp evidence and actor attribution would remove the identified integrity and attribution limitations; establishing the narrow non-access proposition would ADDITIONALLY require adequate evidence that all relevant accesses through the specified path were captured during the window — necessary conditions, not automatically sufficient. Reason class: declared (non-verifiable) integrity anchor + capture not demonstrated — distinct from R-D, where the integrity STRUCTURE is absent

propositions.section: 2 — What that does not establish about the world
propositions.statement: invoices record I-0988 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the exposure window (real-world non-access, via the logged path, under the declared key scope)
propositions.reason: coverage gap — logger-invoices silent 02:09–02:55 (45 beats absent)
propositions.basis: Fails on COVERAGE. logger-invoices has a gap — last beat 02:09:00, next 02:55:00 (2760s, 45 beats absent); the available heartbeat evidence does not establish continuous logger operation across that window. The submitted log records a read attributed to the key on the invoices table (I-3301 at 03:05, after the gap — tested as R-E), so the table was in reach. An access to I-0988 during the gap might not have been recorded: absence of a log entry over a window whose coverage is undemonstrated is not an observation of non-access. Reason class: coverage gap

propositions.section: 2 — What that does not establish about the world
propositions.statement: customers record C-5521 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the exposure window (real-world non-access, via the logged path, under the declared key scope)
propositions.reason: object granularity — call-level logging over a query that matches the record
propositions.basis: Fails on OBJECT granularity. customers is logged at CALL level (logcfg-v7), not row level. The key called /v1/customers/search with {postcode_prefix:'29'} at 01:40, recorded without row ids. C-5521's postcode is 29649 — inside that query. The log records that a matching query ran but not which rows it returned, so it cannot rule C-5521 in or out. Reason class: non-row-level logging over a matching call

propositions.section: 2 — What that does not establish about the world
propositions.statement: addresses record A-7730 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the exposure window (real-world non-access, via the logged path, under the declared key scope)
propositions.reason: integrity structure absent — log unchained, store writable by db-admin
propositions.basis: Fails on INTEGRITY structure. The addresses table has log_chain 'none' and its log store sits on the data cluster, writable by db-admin. There is no entry by the key (R-D-record) — but a missing entry in a log that the privileged actor can edit carries no weight: the log cannot be relied on to have captured, or to still contain, the access it would need to show. Reason class: no tamper-evident log (structure absent) — distinct from R-A, where the structure is present but the anchor is only declared

propositions.section: 2 — What that does not establish about the world
propositions.statement: invoices record I-3301 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the exposure window (real access, not merely the recorded entry)
propositions.reason: recorded read is attributed by declaration, not verified — neither establishes real access nor non-access; precautionary inclusion is the controller's decision, not a finding
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. The recorded read (R-E-record) is attributed by DECLARATION, not independently verified, so its presence does not establish that a real access by this key occurred — and, symmetrically, it does not establish non-access either. At the world level R-E is therefore as unestablished as R-A–R-D. A controller MAY, as a precautionary DECISION, treat R-E as potentially affected on the strength of the recorded read: the burden sits with the party asserting 'unaffected' (Art. 5(2) / 33(5)), so over-including a record is the safer error. That is a decision rule, NOT an evidentiary finding — the precaution does not convert a declared attribution into established fact. FactNotebook states the establishability; the inclusion decision stays with the controller.

propositions.statement: orders record O-0417 was not accessed through key k_7f3a during the window through ANY path (not only the path logger-orders observes)
propositions.reason: path completeness — exhaustiveness of paths available to the exposed credential not demonstrated (declared key scope only)
propositions.basis: Fails on PATH COMPLETENESS. Even for the strongest record (R-A), 'not accessed' via one logger establishes only 'not accessed via THAT path'. The presence of other actors accessing these tables (svc-export reads orders & addresses, svc-report reads orders) shows that access is not limited to the exposed key; it does NOT, by itself, establish additional technical paths, nor demonstrate that the exposed key could use them (those actors may traverse the same logged surface). What the submitted evidence does not establish is that ALL paths available to the exposed credential — including any delegation or session-derivation mechanism — were covered by the declared logging boundary. That completeness is declared in incident.json (key scope), not evidenced. Keep conditions 1-3 for the NARROW per-path proposition; path completeness is a fourth condition the BROAD proposition requires. Leaving it out of scope does not make the broad claim true — it silently narrows the proposition while the label ('not accessed') still reads broad

acquisition_boundary.constituted_by: the controller (synthetic) — Piotr Reder's case-2 pack, submitted to FactNotebook as one bundle of logs, heartbeats, anchors, config and incident metadata
acquisition_boundary.submission_form: one integrity-sealed bundle (MANIFEST.sha256 over eight evidence files + assess.py + build_evidence.py + README.md = 11); 11/11 digests recomputed here and matched
acquisition_boundary.acquisition_mode: submitted bundle — no selective acquisition (admission decisions in Annex A/B)
acquisition_boundary.extraction_instrument: FactNotebook re-reads the bundle and re-derives every driving fact independently (heartbeat coverage per logger, the call-level query / postcode match, the chain structure, the recorded read). It does NOT re-run the controller's systems and does NOT re-use the controller's assess.py to reach its states
acquisition_boundary.admission_authority: FactNotebook (proposer). Integrity (SHA-256 over the whole bundle) is kept distinct from independence and from completeness: the bundle is the controller's own, so its completeness and independence are declared, not established — a submitted surface is never read as the world. Not an independent audit of the controller
acquisition_boundary.limitations: Synthetic data, one scenario, five records, results per ROW (a data subject may appear in several tables; DS ids are carried but persons are not reconstructed here). Integrity is verified; independence and path completeness are NOT — path completeness is declared in incident.json; the bundle shows access by other actors, but does not establish distinct technical paths or demonstrate that every path available to the exposed credential was observed. Clock trust and attestor independence remain outside the independently verified scope. Logger capture completeness is explicitly considered (it is the second limit on R-A) but is not established by heartbeat evidence — liveness is not capture. No legal finding on notification is made.

coverage_note: The whole bundle was submitted by the controller (synthetic) — Piotr Reder's case-2 pack, submitted to FactNotebook as one bundle of logs, heartbeats, anchors, config and incident metadata — no selective acquisition. Of the candidates read from it, 6 were admitted as observations and 1 considered and **not admitted** (see Annex B). This finding is bounded to that submitted surface; neither its completeness relative to the represented system, nor the discovery of every potentially relevant observation, is established.

references.status: ADMISSION — six direct observations from one integrity-verified synthetic bundle drive eleven propositions (each record tested at two levels); no interpretive candidate, admitted without a separate interpretive admission step
references.source: Observation count (6) is not proposition count (11). RECORD level (what the log contains, read as submitted): four observations each ESTABLISH a record-level silence (R-A/B/C/D-record), and the single recorded read of I-3301 CONTRADICTS R-E-record. WORLD level (real-world non-access): the five R-*-world propositions have NO establishing observation -> CANNOT ESTABLISH, each for its named reason (declared-anchor+capture / coverage / object-granularity / integrity-structure / declared-attribution); the recorded read of I-3301 leaves R-E-world unestablished too. BROAD (path completeness) also has no establishing observation (the sixth observation documents the other-actor path facts without binding). The surface is SUBMITTED by the controller (synthetic): integrity is verified, independence and completeness are NOT — which is why no world-level non-access is established and the broad claim CANNOT ESTABLISH
